about.headline: About Me
short_paragraphs: I am an AI Engineer with end-to-end expertise spanning machine learning, generative AI, LLM engineering, deep learning, AI infrastructure, and systems software. My engineering philosophy centers on bridging rigorous mathematical modeling with production-grade performance—taking AI problems from first-principles formulation to distributed training, GPU acceleration, and low-latency deployment.

Currently at Valeo, I work as a Perception Engineer developing camera-based 3D object detection models (DLA-34 backbones) for ADAS, while optimizing deep learning pipelines using TF32, cuDNN benchmarking, and asynchronous data transfers. Previously at Wipro, I led enterprise Generative AI initiatives—orchestrating LangGraph agentic workflows and DALL-E 3 visual automation—and at HCLTech R&D, I delivered edge-quantized vision systems (OpenVINO, 60 FPS), NeRF 3D reconstructions, and continual learning pipelines.

As an IIT Jodhpur Artificial Intelligence alumnus and author of published research on massive multi-agent systems for long-horizon reasoning (arXiv:2512.08545) and an industrial whitepaper on Automotive Robotics with GenAI Agents, I actively investigate emergent agentic architectures and mentor engineering talent across an 8,000+ member LinkedIn community.

projects.title: ADAS 3D Object Detection & Perception
projects.problem: Accurate 3D spatial object detection and tracking in dynamic automotive environments requires high architectural efficiency, zero memory leak tolerance, and strict latency bounds on embedded platforms.

Implemented rigorous multi-sensor checkpoint selection protocols evaluated across Bird's Eye View (BEV) spatial coordinate frames.
Integrated C++ perception algorithms and tracker modules directly into automotive vehicle runtime execution graphs with Klocwork safety analysis.
impact: Delivered robust spatial scene understanding across complex urban and highway scenarios.
Achieved strict memory and determinism compliance verified through Klocwork static analysis.
Streamlined multi-camera evaluation into unified BEV spatial coordinate metrics.

projects.title: High-Throughput Deep Learning Pipeline & GPU Optimization

Optimized GPU execution by enabling TensorFloat-32 (TF32) matrix arithmetic and cuDNN autotuner benchmarking for convolutional layers.
Engineered asynchronous host-to-device memory transfers using pinned CUDA memory streams and efficient TFRecord binary ingestion.

Reduced epoch training wall-clock time through asynchronous data staging.
Standardized multi-worker TFRecord data ingestion across deep perception training jobs.

projects.title: NeRF-based 3D Scene Reconstruction
projects.problem: High-fidelity 3D reconstruction of indoor environments traditionally requires costly LiDAR hardware; monocular RGB scans suffer from textureless surfaces and view ambiguities.
approach: Built an end-to-end spatial reconstruction pipeline combining COLMAP Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pose estimation with Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) continuous volumetric representation.
Designed adaptive point-sampling strategies and custom spatial regularization to stabilize rendering on plain walls and specular surfaces.
Implemented mixed-precision training schedules to accelerate volumetric ray marching.
impact: Delivered photorealistic 3D environment models directly from commodity monocular RGB video scans.
Cut NeRF model training convergence time by 25% through mixed-precision optimization.
Enabled accurate in-house equipment placement and spatial planning without dedicated depth sensors.

projects.title: Controllable Face Synthesis with Stable Diffusion & ControlNet
projects.problem: Standard text-to-image diffusion models lack fine spatial control over structural elements like facial landmarks, poses, and geometric contours.
approach: Conditioned Stable Diffusion latent space using ControlNet modules mapped to facial landmark graphs and estimated depth maps.
Engineered dual-conditioning pipelines allowing simultaneous natural language steering and geometric landmark adherence.
Formulated quantitative identity preservation metrics combining LPIPS perceptual similarity and landmark error distances.
impact: Enabled high-precision facial generation and editing with deterministic pose and expression control.
Established an internal foundation for controllable synthetic media generation and identity-preserving anonymization.
Demonstrated fine-grained control with minimal degradation in generative photorealism.

Quantized and optimized the architecture using the OpenVINO toolkit (INT8 calibration and graph fusion) for embedded hardware targets.

impact: Achieved an 83% reduction in model memory footprint via OpenVINO INT8 quantization.
Delivered sustained 60 FPS real-time throughput on low-power edge processors.

projects.title: Continual Learning & Incremental Object Detection
projects.problem: Retraining deep object detectors from scratch on expanding class taxonomies is computationally prohibitive, while naive fine-tuning suffers from catastrophic forgetting of previously learned classes.
approach: Formulated a dual-distillation continual learning framework combining feature-map distillation and classification logit alignment against a frozen teacher network.
Evaluated memory replay vs. exemplar-free distillation across split COCO benchmark distributions.
Optimized distillation loss balancing factors to equalize representation stability and novel class plasticity.
impact: Sustained ~85% mAP on previously trained base classes while expanding to novel classes.
Achieved detection performance comparable to expensive complete-dataset retraining.
Cut retraining compute expenditure by more than 60%.

Significantly reduced high-frequency facial flickering across phoneme transitions.

publications.title: Curriculum-Guided Massive Multi-Agent System for Long-Horizon Reasoning
publications.abstract: Large Language Models and multi-agent systems show significant promise in decomposing complex tasks, yet they frequently encounter reliability breakdown on long-horizon reasoning tasks alongside escalating computational cost. This work introduces a hierarchical multi-agent architecture that distributes reasoning across a 64×64 grid of lightweight agents supported by a selective oracle. A spatial curriculum progressively expands the operational region of the grid, ensuring agents master easier central subtasks before tackling harder peripheral ones. To maximize decision reliability, the framework integrates Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) as a confidence calibration metric, enabling the curriculum to prioritize regions where agents are both accurate and calibrated. An adaptive Thompson Sampling curriculum manager selects training zones based on competence and NLL reward feedback, demonstrating marked stability improvements on the Tower of Hanoi long-horizon benchmark.
contributions: Hierarchical 64×64 grid multi-agent architecture that distributes complex reasoning while mitigating computational overhead.
Spatial curriculum learning mechanism progressively expanding agent competence boundaries from core subtasks to peripheral challenges.
Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) confidence calibration preventing overconfident hallucinations during multi-step reasoning.
Thompson Sampling curriculum manager adaptively choosing training zones to optimize sample efficiency.
Demonstrated sustained task completion stability and reduced oracle dependency on the Tower of Hanoi long-horizon benchmark.

publications.title: Robotics Meets GenAI Agents: Enabling Robust Long-Horizon Intelligence in Automotive Manufacturing
authors: Indrajit Kar (GM & Head of Advanced AI, Wipro)
Kalathur Chenchu Kishore Kumar (Former Senior AI Engineer, Wipro)
publications.abstract: A comprehensive industrial white paper presenting an architectural blueprint for integrating Generative AI Agents, hierarchical spatial curriculum learning, and multimodal vision intelligence into automotive manufacturing robotics. Traditional industrial robots excel at repetitive, deterministic operations but struggle with multi-stage long-horizon tasks, dynamic part variations, and unforeseen execution anomalies. This work details how multi-agent LLM systems with confidence calibration eliminate error compounding, enable real-time anomaly remediation, and bridge foundational AI research with physical robotic manufacturing lines.
contributions: Architectural blueprint deploying hierarchical multi-agent systems to orchestrate long-horizon robotic manipulation in automotive assembly.
Spatial curriculum learning formulation preventing error cascading and robotic failure propagation across complex multi-step workflows.
Confidence calibration mechanisms that prevent ungrounded LLM hallucinations in mission-critical manufacturing operations.
Multimodal Vision-Language Model integration for zero-shot defect identification, adaptive trajectory replanning, and quality assurance.
